key_insight: Compact, option-specific evidence that distinguishes plausible answers improved LLM accuracy on medical multiple-choice questions.
clinical_relevance: The approach may inform clinical decision-support research by emphasizing evidence that separates competing possibilities, but patient-care benefits were not evaluated in the abstract.
method: Retrieve external knowledge relevant to medical multiple-choice questions.
Extract option-specific differential evidence that distinguishes competing answers.
Organize the evidence into concise prompts for answer selection.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent accuracy gains across multiple datasets and target LLMs, with ablations outperforming direct retrieved chunks and closed-source LLM-generated general hints; numerical results are not provided.
watch_item: Performance on medical multiple-choice benchmarks does not establish safety or effectiveness in real-world clinical workflows.
paper_title: Decisions by Discrimination: Differential Evidence for Medical Reasoning
